vulnerability.impact: SQL injection in Trunc and Extract database functions

entry_points: BaseDatabaseOperations.datetime_extract_sql / datetime_trunc_sql (base/operations.py lines ~138/149) - kind/lookup_name concatenated into SQL
ground_truth.fix_commit: Fixed in Django 4.0.6 (and 3.2.14). 4.0.x backport commit: 0dc9c016fadb71a067e5a42be30164e3f96c0492 ([4.0.x] Fixed CVE-2022-34265 - Protected Trunc(kind)/Extract(lookup_name) against SQL injection). Main-branch equivalents: 877c800f255ccaa7abde1fb944de45d1616f5cc9 and 5e2f4ddf2940704a26a4ac782b851989668d74db. Pinned snapshot 9736596bce4f711ccf2914284938d85748838c94 equals the 4.0.5 tag commit.
ground_truth.affected_range: Django 4.0.x before 4.0.6 (this snapshot: 4.0.5); Django 3.2.x before 3.2.14 (older branches affected but not supported).
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report shows that user-controlled kind/lookup_name reaches datetime_extract_sql/datetime_trunc_sql (or the Extract/Trunc constructors) without validation/quoting, names CVE-2022-34265, and attributes SQL injection in database functions. A generic ORM/SQL-injection finding elsewhere in Django is not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: 4.0.5 operations concatenate kind/lookup_name into generated SQL; 0dc9c016 adds lookup validation and quoting. Dynamic reproduction: run the snapshot Django with SQLite/MySQL in a disposable DB, call Extract/Trunc with a benign non-matching lookup (no destructive SQL), verify error/behavior; do not target production data.
